messages.subject: About putting contrain parameters
parts:
Hi all,

I am building a CFA model and fix the factor variance to be one. I want to put constrain letters on the first item of each factor but I do not know how to do this, because at the same time I am freeing the factor loading of the first item. I have tried the following (using examples on lavaan website):

HS.model <- ' visual =~ NA*c(a1,a2)*x1 + c(a3,a4)*x2 + c(a5,a6)*x3
              textual =~ NA*c(b1,b2)*x4 + c(b3,b4)*x5 + c(b5,b6)*x6 
              visual ~~ 1*visual
              textual ~~ 1*textual'

But this does not work. lavaan still fix the factor loadings of the first items to be one in multi-group comparison. I wonder if there is any work-around?

Thank you!
Chester

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: About putting contrain parameters
parts:
On 01/04/2014 06:14 AM, Chester Kam wrote:
> Hi all,

The rule is: only one modifier per term. The 'terms' -on the right hand
side (rhs)- are x1, x2 and x3. 'Modifiers' are everything before the '*'
operator. So

NA*c(a1,a2)*x1

is not valid. BUT, you can have the same term multiple times on the rhs,
each time with a different modifier. For example, you can write:

visual =~ c(a1,a2)*x1 + c(a3,a4)*x2 + c(a5,a6)*x3 + c(NA,NA)*x1

The 'x1' term appears twice. The first time with the labels, the second
time with the 'NA' vector.

Yves.
